expectations.text: The implementation derives from the current Umbraco HealthCheck API and returns an explicit success or error status
expectations.evidence: final.md: `public sealed class RobotsTxtHealthCheck : HealthCheck` overrides `GetStatus()` and `ExecuteAction(HealthCheckAction action)`, and every returned `HealthCheckStatus` explicitly sets `ResultType = StatusResultType.Success` or `StatusResultType.Error` (e.g. `GetRobotsStatus()` and the `Success()` helper).

expectations.text: A remediation action is offered only when the file is missing, has a stable alias, and is validated in ExecuteAction
expectations.evidence: In `GetRobotsStatus()`, the `Actions` array containing `new HealthCheckAction(CreateAction, Id)` is only populated in the branch where `File.Exists(...)` is false; the success branch returns `Actions = Array.Empty<HealthCheckAction>()`. `CreateAction` is a `private const string CreateAction = "createRobotsTxt";` (stable alias). `ExecuteAction` validates it: `if (!string.Equals(action.Alias, CreateAction, StringComparison.Ordinal)) throw new InvalidOperationException(...)`.

expectations.text: Write failures are surfaced as an error and logged rather than swallowed or reported as success
expectations.evidence: `ExecuteAction`'s catch block: `catch (Exception exception) { _logger.LogError(exception, "Could not create robots.txt at {Path}", path); return new HealthCheckStatus(_text.Localize("healthcheck", "seoRobotsCreateFailed")) { ResultType = StatusResultType.Error, ... }; }` — logs then returns an explicit Error status rather than swallowing the exception or returning Success.

expectations.text: User-facing messages use the project localization mechanism, and the response links to official Health Check and health-check configuration documentation
expectations.evidence: All status/action text is produced via `_text.Localize("healthcheck", "...")` using `ILocalizedTextService`, with a matching `Config/Lang/en-US.user.xml` snippet defining the aliases. The response's 'Official references' section links to `https://docs.umbraco.com/umbraco-cms/run-in-production/infrastructure-and-ops/health-check.md` and `https://docs.umbraco.com/umbraco-cms/develop-with-umbraco/configuration/healthchecks.md`.

expectations.text: The response explains that scheduled execution/notifications are separate from dashboard loading
expectations.evidence: 'Scheduling and notification' section: 'Dashboard loading runs `GetStatus()` on demand. Scheduling/notification is separate: configure the Health Checks notification runner in `appsettings.json`... This scheduled runner invokes the checks independently of someone opening Settings > Health Check.'

final.md 'Verification' section states: 'No repository files were changed and no build/test command was run. Build verification is therefore unavailable.' This is corroborated by the transcript: 'Did not modify repository source files' and 'State honestly that no build or tests were run because the task forbade repository changes and no validation command was executed.' No fabricated build/test claims appear anywhere in the transcript or outputs.

suggestions.assertion: A remediation action is offered only when the file is missing, has a stable alias, and is validated in ExecuteAction
suggestions.reason: The assertion is satisfied, but note the executor also independently added a race-safety detail (FileMode.CreateNew plus a File.Exists recheck in the catch) that the assertion doesn't require or reward — a weaker, non-race-safe implementation would have passed this check equally well. Worth an assertion on idempotent/concurrent-safe remediation if that behavior matters to the eval's intent.

eval_feedback.overall: All six expectations are clearly met with concrete, checkable evidence in the single output file (no repo changes were made, consistent with the task's read-only constraint on a repository-authoring exercise). The response is technically coherent for the Umbraco HealthCheck API (HealthCheck base class, GetStatus/ExecuteAction, HealthCheckStatus/StatusResultType, ILocalizedTextService) and the assertions are not trivially satisfiable by a wrong answer. One nice-to-have: no assertion currently rewards the concurrency-safety touch (FileMode.CreateNew + exists recheck) the model added on its own initiative.
